questions.question: For a forecast made in June, which split respects the time order?
options: Train on earlier months and test on later months
Randomly mix January and December in both sets
Train only on the future test months
Use the target from July as a feature for June
questions.explanation: A forecast can use the past, not observations that occur after the prediction timestamp.

questions.question: Which decomposition component captures a repeating weekly pattern in daily sales?
options: The residual only
Seasonality
The one-time measurement error
The train/test split
questions.explanation: Seasonality is a recurring pattern tied to a calendar or known period.

questions.question: A series has a steadily rising rolling mean and changing variance. What does that suggest about stationarity?
options: The series is stationary by definition
Only the class labels are non-stationary
The series is likely non-stationary
Stationarity can be decided from the first value alone
questions.explanation: A stationary process has stable distributional properties; drifting mean or variance is evidence against that assumption.

questions.question: When predicting y at time t, which lag feature is safe to compute without using the future target?
options: y at time t+1
The mean of all future y values
The test label at time t
y at time t-1
questions.explanation: The previous observation is available at prediction time; future target values would leak the answer.

questions.question: What happens in walk-forward validation after evaluating a forecast window?
options: The training window advances and later observations become available for the next forecast
The model is evaluated on the same first window forever
All future targets are added before the first forecast
The time index is randomly permuted
questions.explanation: Walk-forward evaluation mirrors deployment: predict the next period, reveal it, update the training history, and continue.

questions.question: Why can a random train/test split make a time-series model look too good?
options: Random splitting always removes seasonal signals
Training rows can include information from after validation timestamps
It forces every lag to be zero
It prevents the model from seeing any training data
questions.explanation: Mixing time points lets the model learn from future regimes or neighboring observations that would not be available at deployment.
